question: Type 1 diabetes mellitus in children results from autoimmune T-cell-mediated destruction of pancreatic beta cells, leading to absolute insulin deficiency.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. Unlike T2DM (insulin resistance + relative deficiency), T1DM is caused by autoimmune destruction of beta cells, resulting in absolute insulin deficiency. Without exogenous insulin, lipolysis and ketogenesis proceed unchecked, causing DKA.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. T1DM is an organ-specific autoimmune disease. Autoantibodies (anti-GAD, anti-IA-2, anti-insulin, anti-ZnT8) are detectable in the serum; destruction of beta cells leads to absolute, not relative, insulin deficiency — hence the requirement for exogenous insulin for survival.
